# Draft:Battle of Dukagjin region (1998–1999)

----
The Battle of the Dukagjin region refers to a series of armed clashes and military operations between the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) and Yugoslav Army (VJ) and Serbian police (MUP) forces during the Kosovo War from 1998 to 1999. The fighting took place primarily in western Kosovo, including rural and mountainous areas around Deçan, Junik, Gllogjan, and surrounding villages.

Background
During 1998, the Dukagjin region emerged as one of the strongest areas of KLA activity. The region’s terrain and proximity to the Albanian border facilitated guerrilla warfare, supply routes, and movement of fighters. As violence escalated across Kosovo, Yugoslav security forces launched repeated operations aimed at suppressing KLA presence in the area.
Fighting
The conflict in Dukagjin consisted mainly of ambushes, counteroffensives, and localized battles rather than a single decisive engagement. Yugoslav forces carried out large-scale offensives against villages suspected of supporting the KLA, while KLA units resisted through defensive positions and hit-and-run tactics. Despite these operations, Yugoslav forces were unable to fully eliminate KLA activity in the region, and fighting continued intermittently into 1999.
Nato intervention
Following the start of the NATO air campaign in March 1999, Yugoslav operations in the Dukagjin region were increasingly constrained. KLA units expanded their activity in several areas as Yugoslav forces focused on avoiding air strikes and protecting key infrastructure.
Aftermath
The fighting in the Dukagjin region ended in June 1999 after the Kumanovo Agreement, which led to the withdrawal of Yugoslav forces from Kosovo. The region subsequently came under the control of international peacekeeping forces (KFOR), while the KLA was later demilitarized under international supervision.
